narrative.overview:
Datafore presents as a strategic partner to allied health clinic leaders, not a tool vendor. The site reads like a well-made brief from a serious advisory firm: a confident point of view set in a literary serif, on a white page, with the deep navy of the Datafore wordmark carrying the weight and the logo's bright blue doing the pointing.

It speaks to clinic owners first and to evaluators — partners, funders, procurement panels — second, so governance, status and company facts are always one click away and stated plainly. Credibility comes from restraint and candour: Datafore is pre-customer, and the site never implies otherwise.

Anti-references: the generic SaaS analytics landing page, the earlier teal-and-mono Clinical Loop identity (too technical, too tactical), and the brass registry identity before it (too legal).
keyCharacteristics: White paper and mist grounds, with full-bleed navy bands for the strategic statements.
Source Serif 4 for every heading and statement; Public Sans for everything functional.
Signal blue as the only accent, used for underlines, rules and the current state — never a fill.
Hairline rules and twelve-column asymmetry instead of cards; no shadows or gradients.
One authored motion moment: the hero settles into place.
Graphics are authored, not stock: an illustrative Snapshot excerpt, an engagement cycle and a system diagram, all sharing the logo's arrow.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal blue is the only colour besides navy and the neutrals, and it never fills a surface.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor
rules.body: graphite-600 is the lightest text on light grounds and navy-300 on navy. navy-400 is never text on white.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Nothing sits above a heading to introduce it: no kicker, category label or section number.

rules.name: The Full-Stop Rule
rules.body: Section headlines are sentences that make a claim, and end with a full stop.

rules.name: The Flat Rule
rules.body: No shadows, gradients or blur. Depth comes from the ground changing between bands.

dos: Do state Datafore's status plainly: in development, forming a founding cohort in British Columbia.
Do phrase security and privacy as what the platform is designed to do, not as certifications held.
Do name the real systems — Jane App, Cliniko, Owl Practice, HubSpot.
Do describe benchmarking in the future tense.
Do label illustrative figures as illustrative, in place.
Do route internal links and public/ assets through withBase().
donts: Don't claim clinics, customers, results or testimonials that don't exist.
Don't publish pricing, ARR/CAC/LTV, grants, or roadmap detail.
Don't build the page from cards, or add shadows or gradients.
Don't put a kicker or number above a heading.
Don't use monospace, or signal blue as a fill.
Don't set text in navy-400 on light grounds.
